refutes.statement: Reduction (a) at a fixed key: for a key (g, x) of a strict profile with fewest frozen agents f = 1 (x frozen on its top g), remove x and g, apply Theorem Z' to I' = I - x - g, reinsert x with {g}; i.e. every key has a completable configuration. Refuted: 'A key can be hopeless' - the key (5, 0) has no completable configuration at all (the keys (5, 1) and (5, 2) have one).

witness.source text: There x = 0 has two private goods, which are worthless in I'. With omega = 1, one of them must enter the pool, and every free-valid owner's pair holds another good of x.

notes: Instance A1 (k4/c4min_reduce.md §4.1; attempts/k4-c4min-reduce-a.md). 'smallest n = 3, and m = 2n = 6, omega = 1' (at n = 2 every key works). Replay (both implementations, k4/red_lib.py and k4/red.c): 'key (5, 0) has no completable configuration (Python) yes', 'C: key_noncompletable = 1 yes', ALL CONFIRMED (rerun here). Scratch check with red_lib: key (5,0) has 4 configurations, 0 completable; keys (5,1), (5,2) have 2 configurations each, all completable. 'core N' = 0-based position in the file's 'cores' list (not its 'idx' field). The same core (with other values) is adaptive-p1 of PR #44.
